name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 173 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 173 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: In Kashmir, the senior superintendent of police in Srinagar has ordered intensified security checks, expedited criminal case disposal, and a crackdown on drug and organized crime networks. The police chief of Jammu and Kashmir held a high level security review meeting focusing on intelligence sharing and area domination across the valley. In Manipur, tribal students warned of intensified agitation demanding scholarship releases, while security forces recovered a Maoist weapon dump in Bijapur forests of Chhattisgarh and killed a suspected KCP cadre. Lateef Bhat was killed in Kulgam and security officials said the ISI is planning fresh attacks in Jammu and Kashmir; 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: I Kashmir har senior superintendant for politi i Srinagar beordret intensiverte sikkerhetskontroller, raskere behandling av straffesaker og en nedslag på narkotika‑ og organisert kriminalitet. Politiesjefen i Jammu og Kashmir holdt et høyt nivå sikkerhetsmøte med fokus på etterretningsdeling og dominans i dalen. I Manipur advarte stamme-studenter om intensivering av protester for å kreve utbetaling av stipender, mens sikkerhetsstyrker fant et maoistisk våpenlager i Bijapur-skogene i Chhattisgarh og drepte en mistenkt KCP-medlem. Lateef Bhat ble drept i Kulgam, og sikkerhetsmyndighetene sa at ISI planlegger nye angrep i Jammu og Kashmir; 437 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
